If you live in the US, places like HomeGoods have those small steaming pitchers or similar tall metal mugs you can use as milk steaming receptacles. They're generally dirt cheap, since it's just aluminum (copper mule mugs work too).

Dimensions of milk-based coffee drinks tends to change if you mix up the ratios and technique a bit, I would highly suggest experimenting! Again, to each their own, I'm a black-like-my-soul coffee person myself but I enjoy a latte now and again. I find that steaming the milk for too long tends to create a more "gritty" and sour mouth feel from the milk (best way I can describe it) so if that was the sensation, that may be why you didn't enjoy it that much. Oversteaming can easily happen when you have to make multiple small batches like you described. Milk steaming tends to bring out the sweeter dimensions of the milk (SCIENCE!: Lactose [the naturally occurring sugar in milk] is not very soluble at room or refrigeration temperatures and so has a very neutral taste in terms of sweetness; warming milk and introducing air makes the lactose in the milk more soluble, thereby sweeter) so you can actually control the milk flavor and mouth feel of the latte with practice. What makes steamed milk and espresso a good pairing is exactly this sweet/bitter pairing, which is why it seems a lot of people prefer lattes to straight drip/french press/etc. (don't shoot me, fam).

Since you asked, when I prepare it, it tends to be 1 part foam, 1 part espresso, two parts milk, which I think is a good balance since it avoids one flavor overwhelming the other.

Good luck!
